info.name: Renovation Tracker API
info.description:
Every workflow of the Renovation Project Tracker backend, ordered for a walkthrough.

**Setup**: `docker compose up -d`, `pnpm db:migrate`, `pnpm db:seed`, `pnpm dev` and `pnpm dev:worker`. The collection targets `{{baseUrl}}` (default http://localhost:4000).

**Order**: run folder 1 (the three logins) first; they save the tokens. Then folders 2 to 7 in order: each request saves the ids and cursors the next ones need (jobId, jobVersion, messageCursor, reportId, downloadUrl). Folder 8 streams subscriptions over SSE.

**Auth**: the collection sends Alice's token by default. Requests that act as Bob (homeowner) or Dave (another contractor) override the token; the ones expected to fail without a token use no auth.

**Errors**: the API answers standard GraphQL errors with a stable `extensions.code`: UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, VALIDATION. Requests whose name ends with a code in parentheses are expected to fail with it, and their tests assert it.

item.name: 0. Health
item.description: Liveness of the GraphQL layer. No token needed.

graphql.query: query { health }

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Run the three logins first. Tokens and user ids are saved into collection variables and reused by every other request.

graphql.query: mutation Login($email: String!, $password: String!) { login(email: $email, password: $password) { token user { id name role } } }
mutation Login($email: String!, $password: String!) { login(email: $email, password: $password) { token user { id name role } } }

request.description: Dave owns nothing. Used by the access-control folder to show isolation between contractors.

graphql.query: mutation Login($email: String!, $password: String!) { login(email: $email, password: $password) { token user { id name role } } }
query { me { id email name role } }
mutation { login(email: "alice@contractor.test", password: "wrong") { token } }
query { me { id } }

item.name: 2. Jobs
item.description: Create a job as Alice, then edit it with optimistic locking and share it with Bob. jobId and jobVersion are saved for the following requests.

graphql.query: mutation CreateJob($input: CreateJobInput!) { createJob(input: $input) { id description status costCents version deletedAt canUndo canRedo location { addressLine1 addressLine2 city state postalCode country } contractor { name } homeowners { id name email } } }

request.description: Defaults applied by the server: status PLANNING, country US, version 1. Saves jobId and jobVersion.

graphql.query: query { jobs { id description status costCents version deletedAt canUndo canRedo location { addressLine1 addressLine2 city state postalCode country } contractor { name } homeowners { id name email } } }

query Job($id: ID!) { job(id: $id) { id description status costCents version deletedAt canUndo canRedo location { addressLine1 addressLine2 city state postalCode country } contractor { name } homeowners { id name email } } }

mutation UpdateJob($id: ID!, $input: UpdateJobInput!) { updateJob(id: $id, input: $input) { id description status costCents version deletedAt canUndo canRedo location { addressLine1 addressLine2 city state postalCode country } contractor { name } homeowners { id name email } } }

request.description: expectedVersion is the version last read. The pre-request script turns the saved string into a number. Saves the new jobVersion.

item.name: Update job with a stale version (CONFLICT)

graphql.query: mutation UpdateJob($id: ID!, $input: UpdateJobInput!) { updateJob(id: $id, input: $input) { id version } }

request.description: Run after the first update. The error carries expectedVersion and currentVersion.

item.name: Update job with nothing to change (VALIDATION)

graphql.query: mutation UpdateJob($id: ID!, $input: UpdateJobInput!) { updateJob(id: $id, input: $input) { id } }
mutation AddHomeowner($jobId: ID!, $email: String!) { addHomeowner(jobId: $jobId, email: $email) { id homeowners { id name email } } }

request.description: Idempotent: running it twice is a no-op. Adding a contractor email is a VALIDATION error, an unknown email is NOT_FOUND.

exec: pm.test("Bob is a homeowner of the job", () => pm.expect(body.data.addHomeowner.homeowners.map(h => h.email)).to.include("bob@homeowner.test"));

graphql.query: mutation AddHomeowner($jobId: ID!, $email: String!) { addHomeowner(jobId: $jobId, email: $email) { id } }
query { jobs { id description status costCents contractor { name } } }

exec: pm.test("Bob sees the shared job", () => pm.expect(body.data.jobs.map(j => j.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("jobId")));

item.name: 3. Messages
item.description: The chat log between Alice and Bob. Keyset cursors keep pages stable while new messages arrive.

graphql.query: mutation SendMessage($jobId: ID!, $body: String!) { sendMessage(jobId: $jobId, body: $body) { id body createdAt sender { name role } } }
mutation SendMessage($jobId: ID!, $body: String!) { sendMessage(jobId: $jobId, body: $body) { id body createdAt sender { name role } } }
mutation SendMessage($jobId: ID!, $body: String!, $clientMessageId: ID) { sendMessage(jobId: $jobId, body: $body, clientMessageId: $clientMessageId) { id body clientMessageId } }

request.description: Run it twice: the second run returns the same message id instead of creating a duplicate. The test compares with the previous run.

exec: if (previous) pm.test("retry returned the same message", () => pm.expect(body.data.sendMessage.id).to.eql(previous));

graphql.query: query Messages($jobId: ID!, $first: Int) { job(id: $jobId) { messages(first: $first) { edges { cursor node { id body createdAt sender { name } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } } }
query Messages($jobId: ID!, $first: Int, $after: String) { job(id: $jobId) { messages(first: $first, after: $after) { edges { node { body sender { name } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } } }
query Latest($jobId: ID!) { job(id: $jobId) { messages(last: 20) { edges { node { body createdAt sender { name } } } pageInfo { hasPreviousPage startCursor } } } }
query Messages($jobId: ID!) { job(id: $jobId) { messages(first: 500) { edges { node { id } } } } }

item.name: 4. History, undo and redo
item.description: Every change is an append-only entry. Undo and redo are linear and contractor-only; homeowners read the timeline.

graphql.query: query History($jobId: ID!) { job(id: $jobId) { version canUndo canRedo history(first: 50) { edges { cursor node { seq kind targetSeq supersededAt createdAt actor { name } changes { field before after } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } } }

request.description: Expect CREATED, HOMEOWNER_ADDED and the UPDATED entries, each with before/after per field.

graphql.query: mutation Undo($jobId: ID!) { undoJobChange(jobId: $jobId) { id description status costCents version deletedAt canUndo canRedo location { addressLine1 addressLine2 city state postalCode country } contractor { name } homeowners { id name email } } }

request.description: Reverts the most recent applied change and bumps the version. Check the timeline afterwards: a new UNDONE entry points at what it reverted.

graphql.query: mutation Redo($jobId: ID!) { redoJobChange(jobId: $jobId) { id description status costCents version deletedAt canUndo canRedo location { addressLine1 addressLine2 city state postalCode country } contractor { name } homeowners { id name email } } }
mutation Undo($jobId: ID!, $expectedVersion: Int) { undoJobChange(jobId: $jobId, expectedVersion: $expectedVersion) { id version canUndo canRedo } }

item.name: Edit after undo (supersedes the redo stack)

graphql.query: mutation UpdateJob($id: ID!, $input: UpdateJobInput!) { updateJob(id: $id, input: $input) { id costCents version canUndo canRedo } }

request.description: Afterwards the timeline shows the discarded entry with supersededAt set. Nothing is deleted.

graphql.query: mutation Redo($jobId: ID!) { redoJobChange(jobId: $jobId) { id } }
query History($jobId: ID!) { job(id: $jobId) { history(first: 50) { edges { node { seq kind actor { name } changes { field before after } } } } } }
mutation Undo($jobId: ID!) { undoJobChange(jobId: $jobId) { id } }

item.name: 5. Reports
item.description: Asynchronous PDF export: request, poll until COMPLETED, download through the presigned URL. The worker must be running.

graphql.query: mutation RequestReport($jobId: ID!) { requestReport(jobId: $jobId) { id status attempts createdAt } }
query Report($id: ID!) { report(id: $id) { id status attempts error downloadUrl startedAt completedAt job { id description } requestedBy { name } } }

request.description: Run again until status is COMPLETED. Saves downloadUrl, a presigned S3 link valid for 15 minutes.

exec: pm.test("status is a known value", () => pm.expect(["PENDING", "PROCESSING", "COMPLETED", "FAILED"]).to.include(report.status));

request.description: Opens the presigned URL saved by the previous request. In Postman use Send and Download to save the file, or paste the URL in a browser.

item.name: 6. Access control
item.description: What other users see. Anything invisible answers NOT_FOUND; a role mismatch answers FORBIDDEN.

graphql.query: query Job($id: ID!) { job(id: $id) { id } }
query { jobs { id } }
mutation UpdateJob($id: ID!, $input: UpdateJobInput!) { updateJob(id: $id, input: $input) { id } }
mutation RequestReport($jobId: ID!) { requestReport(jobId: $jobId) { id } }
query Report($id: ID!) { report(id: $id) { id } }
query { job(id: "not-a-uuid") { id } }

item.name: 7. Soft delete and restore
item.description: Deleting freezes the job and hides it from lists; undo brings it back.

graphql.query: mutation RemoveHomeowner($jobId: ID!, $homeownerId: ID!) { removeHomeowner(jobId: $jobId, homeownerId: $homeownerId) { id homeowners { email } } }

request.description: Idempotent. Afterwards Bob gets NOT_FOUND for this job.

graphql.query: mutation DeleteJob($id: ID!, $expectedVersion: Int) { deleteJob(id: $id, expectedVersion: $expectedVersion) { id deletedAt version canUndo } }
mutation UpdateJob($id: ID!, $input: UpdateJobInput!) { updateJob(id: $id, input: $input) { id } }
query { jobs { id description deletedAt } }
query { jobs(includeDeleted: true) { id description deletedAt } }
mutation Undo($jobId: ID!) { undoJobChange(jobId: $jobId) { id deletedAt version canUndo canRedo } }

item.name: 8. Real time
item.description: GraphQL subscriptions. The WebSocket transport (graphql-ws) is what clients use; Postman can stream the same subscription over Server-Sent Events with a GET request.

query.value: subscription { messageAdded(jobId: "{{jobId}}") { body createdAt sender { name } } }

request.description:
Send this request and keep it open; Postman shows each event as it arrives. Then run "Send message as Alice" from folder 3 in another tab. Bob must be a homeowner of the job.

For WebSocket, use Postman's GraphQL request type (New > GraphQL) or GraphiQL at {{baseUrl}}/graphql with the connection params {"authorization": "Bearer <token>"}.
Open right after "Request report" and watch PROCESSING and COMPLETED arrive from the worker through Redis.
